llm.summary: The skill is coherent for managing ImageKit, but its setup path can run an unverified remote installer script, so it belongs in Review.

dimensions.detail: Runtime authority is mostly constrained to Bash(oo *) and the OOMOL ImageKit connector, but the documented fallback installer would exceed that narrow runtime surface if followed.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: First-time setup instructs running remote installer commands with pipe-to-shell patterns on macOS/Linux and Windows when oo is missing, without version pinning, checksum verification, or explicit user confirmation.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The trigger language is broad for ImageKit-related tasks, but it remains scoped to ImageKit and includes user-confirmation requirements for state-changing and destructive actions.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill does not ship bundled executable code or persistence hooks, but installing the oo CLI and signing into OOMOL are cross-session setup steps with account-level implications.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The skill's stated purpose, allowed tool pattern, and action list fit ImageKit management through the OOMOL oo CLI; delete and purge actions are disclosed as destructive and require explicit approval.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with OOMOL mediating ImageKit actions and with the oo CLI setup. Prefer installing the CLI manually from trusted documentation and verifying the installer before use; approve delete_file or purge_cache only after checking the exact target and payload.
llm.findings:
[SC2] unexpected: A CLI dependency is coherent with the skill, but the artifact-backed pipe-to-shell installer instructions are higher impact than necessary and lack integrity checks or clear user-directed control.
[SQP-1] expected: The broad ImageKit trigger is real, but the artifact still confines use to ImageKit operations and separately requires approval before destructive actions, so this is a scoping note rather than the main Review reason.
